target_claim: Running Dijkstra's algorithm (with the re-insertion priority queue the solution specifies) on the explicitly constructed DAG family Gn performs Omega(2^n) successful Relax operations.
source_quote:
Theorem 1. When Dijkstra’s algorithm processes Gn starting from source s, it performs
Ω(2n) successful Relax operations.
test_sketch: Build Gn exactly as specified (lines 17-35: s->v1,b weight 0; vi,0->vi+1,b weight +2^i; vi,1->vi+1,b weight -2^i+1; vn-1,b->t weight 0). Run Dijkstra with a re-insertion priority queue (the variant the solution names on lines 97-99), instrumenting a counter for Relax calls and successful relaxations. For n=2..12 the measured successful-relaxation counts are 3,7,11,...,4n-5 (linear), e.g. 43 at n=12 versus the claimed >= c*2^12 = c*4096; the ratio count/2^n tends to 0, refuting the Omega(2^n) lower bound. The failure mechanism: edge weights depend only on the source vertex and the all-ones (negative) prefix is also the minimum-distance prefix at every level, so Dijkstra settles each vertex O(1) times and never re-relaxes exponentially.
